output.name: Murhal
output.myth: In the cold month, when the boats were hauled up, a sea-duck built her nest on the skerry above the tideline. She had no reeds, only her own breast. She plucked it bare, one feather at a time, and lined a cradle of driftwood with the warm down for her eggs. When the chicks hatched, Tavo came roaring to tear it all away. The hen did not lift. She sat through the gale with her wings spread over the babies, and the wind wore itself out on her back. Ennu, watching from the Upper Sea, sent a gull with a bone needle so she could stitch her torn cloak of feathers. Mother Hesk, at the pole, counted every chick and every feather. When the hen went aloft as a star, the Reel kept her where the warm feathers are counted. On cold nights the Ilvari ask her for a little warmth. She will lend it, but she wants the count kept true.
output.verse:
She plucked her breast bare
to line the chicks' cold cradle
Hesk counts each warm down
